_comment: Mutations that remove the guarantee added by the fix for the $499
'Managed' tier: a customer on the TOP tier must never be shown an
upgrade prompt.
The chrome used to ask `user.plan !== "pro"` to decide whether to show
the upgrade affordances. That was correct while 'pro' was the top tier;
the $499 tier sits ABOVE it, so the question became wrong and a customer
who paid $499 was told to upgrade four times (the 'Upgrade to PRO' entry
in the user menu, the amber crown, the amber styling and the 'Upgrade
plan' tooltip).
The frontend receives the RAW plan key: `/users/me` returns the ORM user
(api/depthsight_api.py:1874) and the login response is
`schemas.User.model_validate(user_db)` (api/routes/auth.py:187). The
server resolves the legacy `premium` key onto `managed` at READ time
(api/plans.py `resolve_plan_key`) and the rows are NOT migrated, so
'premium' is a key the frontend really sees -- B mutants cover it.
A is the tier list: without 'managed' in it, a Managed customer is
nagged again. B is the legacy alias: without it, a legacy `premium`
customer is nagged again. C is the decision itself: with it, the upsell
for a customer who CAN still upgrade is gone -- the other half of the
guarantee. D, E, F and G are the four places the decision is used, each
one re-spelled as the old `user.plan !== "pro"`.
Run with:  python tools/mutation_harness.py tools/mutations/managed_upgrade_prompt.json
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.

mutations.label: A: the Managed tier is no longer a top tier
B: the legacy premium key no longer resolves onto managed
C: nobody is ever shown an upgrade prompt again
mutations.needle:
export const showsUpgradePrompt = (plan?: string | null): boolean =>
	!hasProfessionalTierAccess(plan);
mutations.replace:
export const showsUpgradePrompt = (plan?: string | null): boolean =>
	false;

mutations.label: D: the user menu nags a Managed customer again
E: the plan badge shows the upgrade crown to a Managed customer again
F: the plan badge tooltip says 'Upgrade plan' to a Managed customer again
G: the plan badge is styled as an upgrade target for a Managed customer again
